title: Podium

idea.rule: sort() lines them up smallest first — the trophy sits at the END of the line.
idea.detail: scores.sort() rearranges the list in place from smallest to biggest. After that, index 0 is the lowest score and the highest is at the very end. Negative indexes count from the back, so scores[-1] is the last one — the best.

model_restatement: Find the highest score and print it.

clarify.question: What if two scores tie for best?
clarify.answer: Then that score is still the best — print it once.

clarify.question: What if there are no scores?
clarify.answer: There's always at least one score today.

clarify.question: Can I change the order of the list?
clarify.answer: Sorting the list in place is fine today.

clarify.question: Can I just use max()?
clarify.answer: max() would do it — here, use sort so we can watch the line-up.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Sort the scores, take the first one, and announce it.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 2, what is best?

why_line: sort() puts the smallest first, so scores[0] after sorting is the lowest score — 42.

explain.rule: sort() lines everyone up shortest first — scores[0] grabs the front of the line, which is the lowest score.
explain.bridge: So where in the line is the best score standing?

fix.rule: After sort(), the best is at the very end — scores[-1] counts from the back.

walk.gloss: Line the scores up, smallest first.
Take the last one — the biggest.

alternatives.note: max() skips the sort — the shortcut.
Sort biggest first, then the front is the best.

hints: After line 1, which score is at index 0?
sort() is smallest first. The best is at the other end.

follow_up.prompt: A tie at the top: [9, 9, 1] — what's the best?
follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — sorted, the best is still at the end.

one_liner: sort() lines them up smallest first — the trophy sits at the END of the line.
